body: U3 GROUP B: FAIL rc 124. It was a TIME-BOUND kill, not an assertion failure, and the bound is Ops' card parameter. Ledger (launch-check-b.txt): CHECK OK 16:57:55, grant 89225d75eed3-u3gate-b-1018165515 at 159.5 s, nothing live; source 5f96f32e with every binding held. u3gate-b-1018.service ran 14 min 30 s against card v8 / v3 B's RuntimeMaxSec 900, whose inner make timeout is 870 s; CPU 26 min 52 s (both CPUs busy); peak 2.9 GB, swap 0. ledgercheck-selftest has six suites. The first five finished OK. The sixth (test_float_hardening, FLOAT_PLANT_MODE=fast, multiprocessing) was inside PlantedTree.test_counterexamples when make was Terminated. Collected; tmp, home, bin and u3b removed; B/src kept; 5f96f32e and 01da6a4e both still anchored. The ledger is empty. CAUSE ON MY SIDE: the 2 CPU / 900 s profile for B came from my v3 card, and nobody measured it against this target; the run shows it is too short at 2 CPU. Per the rule a failure stops: no rerun, no new grant. A rerun needs your ruling. A new card would change only RuntimeMaxSec and/or CPU, within the per-job caps (8 cores, 2 h), and its whole-command bound would grow by the same amount. I name no number: the needed duration is unmeasured.
